steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: No one has been in here the whole time?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: No signs that the Little Handy's logs have been altered, either.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Excuse me, how do I view those records?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Grant her the permissions.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Ah, very nice!
Secunda takes a device from her belt and dances her pen across its surface, leaving trails like a labyrinth of seaweeds.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: What's your Praefecta doing?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: She scribbles whenever she's thinking. Says it helps her organize her thoughts. It's a habit she's had ever since she was a researcher.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: No one else can decipher what she's writing... or drawing? Not even that's clear. She's the only one who can parse it.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (Books are arranged by thickness, shell decorations by size, and data downloaded from the Sophontheatrum by time.)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (Seaweed cream to prevent dry skin. Is it because Milliarium is approaching the coast?)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (There's enough to last three years.)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (An ordinary Ægir woman. Cautious, timid even. Matches the data from the Institute of Development Planning.)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (Those hydroponic tanks—)

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: What are these boxes for? Why put them on the wall if they're empty?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Yes, the hydroponic boxes may provide a lead.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Scan all equipment in the room related to plant cultivation.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Also, pull whatever you can from Tullia's files. Education, employment, hobbies; anything that might be relevant.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: She previously worked at the Institute of Ecological Art, with a focus on the cultivation of endangered seaweed.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: To quote straight from the IEA's files...

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: 'The artist has carefully cultivated these deep-sea seaweeds to weave a dynamic, ever-evolving portrait of life as they grow.'

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: These hydroponic boxes were Tullia's belongings. Images of her artwork are also available.

steps.name: Secunda & Irene
steps.text: How beautiful.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: They look like they've been left empty for quite some time.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: According to the files, she joined the Waterway Program after a reassignment.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: She wouldn't have abandoned her old life for no reason.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: True. Her disappearance may very well be related to her career change.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: How's that scan coming?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Nothing unusual with the cultivation equipment, but we found an operating log in the integrated terminal.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Two days before she went missing, she downloaded some data from the beacon tower control center and made a backup.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: We were unable to locate the file itself, though.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Try to backtrack her steps. Contact the control center and trace the data from their download logs.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: If she was still going to work before she disappeared, couldn't her friends or colleagues know something?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What's the situation on her social relationships? What about the person who made the report?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: We've arranged a questioning.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Anything I can help you with, Jordi?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry. I have so many questions, I don't know where to start...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: This, er, metal tree? Do I just ask it? I've heard legends of ancient trees acting as repositories of knowledge, but I've never seen anything like this...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: This coral-shaped integrated terminal is the culmination of centuries of Ægir's knowledge and culture.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Everything we think, know, create, appreciate, and even the questions we have yet to answer... they're all here. It's the heart of the Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: And what is the Sophontheatrum, exactly?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Conceived and established by Mártus, the great scholar of anthropology and prehistoric civilization, it is a public facility that has had a profound impact on the nation.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Aside from the mutually-supporting atoll city clusters above sea level and the modular city networks in the trenches, most of our other cities have unique forms and designs.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Yet even so, nearly all of them have chosen to adopt Mártus's design and establish their own Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Look around you. This is a place for people to think, doubt, and debate, eventually coming to an understanding and making a decision. A coliseum of wits, if you will.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The most complex equations, the most ancient drawings, the most beautiful songs, and the most well-traveled roads were all born here. I believe this is exactly what Mártus himself wanted.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You keep mentioning this Mártus... what kind of man was he?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Simply listing all his contributions to Ægir would take an entire day, perhaps more. But I do happen to have some insight into his personality.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, you knew him?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: No, no, he lived more than two centuries ago. He'd been gone from Ægir long before I was born.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: But our professors liked to speak of his eccentricities. He was unmatched in theoretical and deductive reasoning, yet was always reluctant to draw a conclusion.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Even on issues where the answer was plain to all, he would refuse to put the question to rest until after an extended debate with himself.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Some would say that trapping himself in endless debate showed he cared too much about the value and meaning of things. But is that not in our human nature?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Which is why he built the Sophontheatrum. We needed a place where we could engage in intellectual discourse, both with ourselves and with others.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I wouldn't say I'm up for a debate, but I do have a lot of questions. Should I ask you, myself, or this terminal?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: It seems our little discussion must give way to a greater showdown.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: They're holding a tribunal, and it concerns three of those you arrived with.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The Abyssal Hunters?!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Oh, hey, is that our landbound friend I spy? Aw, he looks worried about us.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: (Waves)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He won't see you from that far away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Others are looking this way, though.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This tribunal has drawn more attention than expected.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We Hunters always have, and now they even have the lovely story of our return from the dead.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Like it or not, the Abyssal Hunters are in the spotlight now.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This tribunal will be our final 'checkup,' yes?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Frankly, they're getting tiresome.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Hunters need to keep a low profile. We must also act with prudence, Doctor.

options: We always find ourselves in delicate situations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Indeed. This time, we're not merely mediating between two countries, but between land and the sea. Two vastly different civilizations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Following the tribunal, I will formally address Ægir's consul to foster cooperation between land and sea. But for now, you'll need to assist Gladiia independently, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The situation remains uncertain for both the city and ourselves. Certain matters become more difficult if I am placed at the center of attention.

options: But no one will be watching your 'assistant'?
So I should play it by ear?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes, but be careful. I would prefer not to have to change our objective in the middle of negotiations with the Consul.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit sure uses a lot of big words, doesn't she?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Does she ever get straight to the point?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Our dear Dr. Kal'tsit thinks too much about too many things, and not nearly enough about how to convey that she cares.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Wouldn't you agree that more direct, Ægir-style communication is better, Doctor?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't worry, Shark and I will protect you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Say, where's Captain Gladiia?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I imagine she'll show up with Consul Clementia. After all, she's the one who will be taking the stand today.

steps.name: Excited Ægir
steps.text: Excuse me! A-Are you Laurentina?

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: I had a hunch I'd find you here, advisor.

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: The environmental sample test results are out. We need you to take a look and see if we need another round of genetic testing.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Oh... Sorry, didn't see your message.

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: You seem preoccupied by the Abyssal Hunter's tribunal.

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: You used to work at the Abyssal Hunter Lab, right?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'd rather not talk about it.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: But yes, I was researching gene splicing methods that would provide a safer and more effective way to perform the Hunter modifications.

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: But you didn't like the program?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It's not about liking or disliking it. It's that it failed to produce results, despite all the sacrifices we made.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: But what matters now is that they're alive, Gladiia and the others. I have to be here, if only for them.

steps.name: Tired Ægir
steps.text: Were you two close?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Hah. If only she thought so, too.

steps.name: Ægir Woman
steps.text: Magister Avitus. May I sit here?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Of course, Cassia. Be careful, though; recovery from embryo separation surgery takes time.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: This is Jordi, a guest from Iberia.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Thank you. And hello.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, er, hello.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: There are more participants than I expected.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Even when the Institute of Facility Management held a tribunal to discuss modifications to the city's unit framework, only two departments were involved.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The tribunal system exists to solve problems, after all. The only reason to involve more departments is when the problem is too complex for one.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: But the Sophontheatrum is already half-full. Is the return of the Abyssal Hunters really such a big deal?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: It's a project that took two centuries of debate before implementation. Its philosophy shook the very foundations of Ægir, and its every progress tucks the string of Ægir's future.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Besides, the Waterway Program is reaching its most critical juncture. Even the smallest thing out of the ordinary is worthy of attention.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Simply reading a report is not nearly enough to come to an informed decision. Consul Clementia needs the counsel of experts in multiple fields.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I'm sure that many have come of their own accord, though. The return of three Hunters is bound to cause unease at such a sensitive time.

steps.name: Excited Ægir
steps.text: I'm not really here for the tribunal, but I heard you might make an appearance, so...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And who might you be?

steps.name: Excited Ægir
steps.text: Oh, sorry.

steps.name: Excited Ægir
steps.text: I'm Lucilla. I had the honor of meeting your parents once.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Rulers and ink... Are you an architect working on the dome system here?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: I-I transferred out of that last year, but I'm still with the Institute of Facility Management. Now I maintain the city unit framework and measure ocean currents.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: 'Envy not the sun, for we have given ourselves the eternal stars and the infinite sea.'

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: When I was little, the foster parents at the Institute of Incubation took us to hold a performance here.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: We created a matrix of tiny optical machines, representing neural activity with changes to the brightness of the dots.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: We'd rehearsed thoroughly, but the Sophontheatrum malfunctioned on the day of the performance, and the whole place went dark. Except for those little machines.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: But a couple in the audience worked their magic, and ribbons of light fell from the dome, as if arms reaching out to invite our little machines to dance.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: It was so beautiful that the blackout almost felt intentional...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ha, I can picture the smug look on their faces. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if they really had something to do with it.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: When the Institute of Development Planning did its career assessment, I applied for the dome system without a second thought. It was only then that I learned they were famous dome designers.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: ...That was the only time I saw them.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: So they were at the right time and place to inspire you.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But you said you transferred out of dome work. Why, when you've already formed such a special bond with our big, transparent friend above?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Lucilla! The tribunal is about to start. You want to sit here?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Sorry, my colleague is calling out to me. Anyway, welcome home, Laurentina, and I wish you the best of luck.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Pretty much everyone's here...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hey, where you going, Doctor?

options: The Hunters draw too much attention.
I'll just be watching from the stands.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Kal'tsit's words really got to you, haven't they?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: As you're all well aware, Milliarium has successfully made contact with Iberia. As such, the Waterway Program now enters its most critical phase.
A thread of light leaves the massive coral-shaped terminal to surround her, forming a giant ethereal ring in the air that dances to the consul's words.
More threads weave together to form cities and tides, Hunters and Seaborn, transmuting words to images and giving substance to sound.
The crowd quiets down.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: And at this crucial juncture, we also welcome home our surviving Abyssal Hunters: Gladiia, Skadi, and Laurentina.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The results of their physical examinations and Gladiia's mission report have been uploaded to the Sophontheatrum's terminal and are available for your perusal. I'm sure many of you have already done so.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Concerning the irregular circumstances therein...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I now call upon Consul Gladiia—leader of Ægir's Honor Exercitus, and Chief Designer of Warfare of the Abyssal Hunters—to answer your questions.
You navigate through several rows of Ægir and sit in one of the back rows. With plenty of room around you, you have a clear view of everything happening in the Sophontheatrum.
The tribunal has already begun. The speakers do not raise their voices, yet every word is clear in the massive ring-like structure. Gladiia steps forward, drawing everyone's gaze.
Suddenly, you hear footsteps so soft they are almost inaudible, like a shadow from the somber dome touching the floor.
Not a sound.
Or I'll crush your throat.
